hypothesis: NFC-stable visible typographic substitutions at internal apostrophe and hyphen sites will change local token identities and the following context-dependent watermark observations without replacing words or sentence structure.
mechanism: SynthID-style context-dependent statistics resynchronize after an isolated edit. Multiple separated retokenization sites should destroy or replace more local observation windows than the sparse contraction-only portfolio while preserving the words read by a person.
experiment: Freeze a detector-blind context-survival plan over the canonical TinyDev corpus, score it in an independent process, compare matched policy and edit-cost cells with the historical v3 plan, and record detection counts, score and margin distributions, observation destruction, control distance, fidelity, and exact replay hashes.

mappings.site: ASCII apostrophe strictly between ASCII letters

normalization_contract: Unicode NFC stable; visible punctuation only; no Cf, Cs, Co, Mn, or Me mutations
protected_content_contract: URLs, email addresses, paths, CLI tokens, quoted spans, identifiers, and caller-protected ranges are never eligible
fidelity_contract: No word insertion, deletion, reordering, semantic substitution, or sentence-structure change
kill_criteria: Reject if the representation differential audit does not show tokenization change across every pinned tokenizer family for at least two independent sources.
Reject if protected-span replay, Unicode NFC, hard invariants, or exact deterministic replay fails.
Reject if the independently scored matched-cost experiment does not improve watermark detection or detector-margin outcomes relative to the historical context-survival plan.
Reject if unwatermarked-control distance or text-fidelity evidence is materially worse than the preregistered development tolerance.
claim_scope: Open weighted-mean SynthID TinyDev engineering evidence only
